# Kition kit rules (read first)

<!-- kition-quality:begin (generated by kition-sdk tools/sync-quality.mjs; edit the template there) -->
## Quality rules (read first)

- Tests are the spec. Read `docs/quality.md` and the feature catalogue (`features.yaml`)
  before changing behaviour. When code and a case disagree, the case wins unless a maintainer
  approves changing the case.
- Before you finish any task, run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`. If it fails, the task is not done. Claude Code
  runs it for you through the Stop hook; agents without hooks (Codex) run it by hand and
  report the real exit code.
- The full checks and tests run on GitHub, in the kit's CI run, not on your machine: a task is
  done only when HEAD has a passing CI run and is on `origin/main`. Use Kition's
  `scripts/kit-ci.sh` (`push`, `wait`, `failures`, `land`; Kition's `docs/kits.md`, section
  4c). Compile only the crates you touched locally.
- Never edit expected results to make a test pass: files under `cases/**/expected/`, paths
  listed under `protected` in `features.yaml`, and the `expected`, `tolerance`, `reference`,
  `input` and `steps` of an existing `case.yaml`. If you believe an expected result is wrong,
  stop and explain why in the task's findings; only a maintainer approves expected-result changes.
- Never weaken a test to make it pass: no deleted or loosened assertions, no added
  `#[ignore]`, `.skip`, `.only` or `.todo`, no raised tolerances. kition-sdk's
  `tools/check-expected.mjs` lists every such change for the maintainers.
- Every bug fix starts with a failing case under `cases/regressions/issue-<n>/`, then the fix.
- Every new feature adds an entry to `features.yaml` and at least one gating test.
- Put the task id and the case ids in the commit message.
- Stage only your own files: `git add` them by name; never `git commit -a` or `git add -A`.
  Other sessions may have uncommitted work in the same checkout.
- Work on `kition-slide` only in its main checkout; never change, build, or commit in its worktrees (`kition-slide-wt/*`, `kition-*-wt`, `kition-naming-work`).
- Never start `cargo xtask eval` (the real-model `layer: eval` cases): only a maintainer starts it (F-QA-16). Write eval cases and check them with `--dry-run`, which calls no model.
- No compatibility layers: no aliases, old names, old file suffixes, migrations, or readers for
  old formats. Delete a replaced path in the same change.
<!-- kition-quality:end -->

This repository is Kition's `kit.sheet` kit. These rules come first; the upstream rules below
still apply to the engine.

- The kit draws **its own editor**: `web/` is a React app on `@kition/sdk/editor` (kition-sdk's
  shared kit UI library) with Kition Sheet's ribbon, formula bar, grid, and sheet tabs; a host
  (Kition, or `web/dev.html` for development) shows it in an iframe and talks to it over the Kit
  UI protocol (`kition-kit-ui/1`, kition-sdk `docs/platform/reference/ui-protocol.md`). Style it only with the
  host's theme tokens and kit-editor components; ribbon labels and command titles are Kition Sheet's
  English text, translated by the i18n catalogs in `web/src/i18n/upstream/` and, where those lack
  a label, by `PHRASES` in
  `web/src/strings.ts` (with the editor's own `en-US` and `zh-CN` strings); take typed text
  through kit-editor's `TextSink`. Files go only through the host.
- `bindings/wasm` compiles the engine to WebAssembly on the public
  `KitionAI/kition-sdk` crate; the editor runs it in a Web Worker. The contract and the Kition platform rules live in kition-sdk
  (`docs/platform/kits/engine.md`, `docs/platform/reference/ui-protocol.md`), the agent protocol
  in KHP (`github.com/kitharness/kitharness`);
  change them there, never here. `kition-sheet-kit` must keep passing `kition_kit::testing::check_contract`,
  and `kit.json` must pass kition-sdk's `tools/check-manifest.mjs`.
- Tools run in the engine (`KitTools`): clicks, drags, headings, typing, and keys select and enter cells through Kition Sheet's own commands (`selection.set`, `selection.move`, `cell.set`), and the selection and the cell being typed return as engine overlays. Never draw editor chrome into the rendered pixels.
- Drawing objects (shapes and text boxes) share their preset outlines, `KitDrawing 1.0` commands
  (`drawing.*`), gestures and ribbon controls with the other Office kits through kition-sdk's
  `kition-office-core` crate and kit-editor's drawing controls; depend on the pinned public SDK,
  never copy them.
- Whatever else doc, sheet and slide all hold (equations, smart graphics, charts, ink, and
  later the PDF and picture export) belongs in `kition-office-core` too: move it there rather
  than keeping a kit's own copy.
- The whole repository is Apache-2.0 ([LICENSE](LICENSE)), including the upstream-derived
  crates; third-party notices are listed in `NOTICE`. Upstream is credited only in `NOTICE`;
  never write upstream names anywhere else.

# Kition Sheet — instructions for agents

Kition Sheet is a clean-room, open-source, Rust-native spreadsheet engine targeting Microsoft Excel parity — and superiority (speed, openness, agent control).

See `docs/kits.md` in the Kition repository and kition-sdk's `docs/platform/` for the conventions shared across kits.

## Start every session here
1. Read `plan/STATUS.md` (current milestone, next task), then the task in `plan/execution-plan.md` and the relevant `plan/architecture.md` section. Behaviour reference: `plan/excel/*.md` (`observed-ui.md` holds measured observations of the running app).
2. Follow the autonomous operation protocol (`plan/execution-plan.md` §7). Don't stop to ask unless §7 lists the decision as the user's.

`plan/` is gitignored (local only).

## Assets and iconography — absolute rule
**No Microsoft, Adobe, Avid, Autodesk (or any other vendor's) iconography, images, artwork, fonts, templates, themes or sample files — ever.** This is the most important rule in this repository; breaking it is a serious failure.
- Every asset in the repo is original work by Kition Sheet contributors, or public domain / CC0, or open source / Creative Commons that allows redistribution (or licensed open source by the contributor who created it).
- Every asset file has a row in [`docs/attribution.md`](docs/attribution.md) (author, source, license). `cargo xtask assets` enforces it. Adding an asset without a row is a bug.
- Prefer art generated in code: table and cell style palettes, themes and sample workbooks are drawn/defined in code and original.
- Never copy Office's icons, ribbon artwork, theme XML, table-style definitions, templates, clip art or wording beyond feature names. Excel feature *names* (menu labels, function names) are fine.
- Screenshots of Microsoft software are never committed (they live only in `plan/excel/screenshots/`).

## Never crash
People trust Kition Sheet with their numbers; a crash loses their work. **This outranks feature work.**
- **No panics in non-test code:** no `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!`, `unimplemented!`; no `unsafe` (`unsafe_code = "forbid"`).
- **Errors are `Result<T, E>`** through the crate's error type and `?`.
- **Input-derived numbers are hostile** (files, formulas, commands, agent params): `get()` instead of indexing, checked/saturating arithmetic, cap input-sized allocations (huge ranges, `REPT`, `SEQUENCE`, whole-column references).
- **Bound recursion** (formula nesting, dependency chains, names referring to names).
- **Last-resort guard:** `Session::execute` catches escaped panics and restores the workbook. It's a safety net, not a license.
- **Prove it:** every crash fix lands with a regression test (`tests::every_command_survives_empty_params` fuzzes every command).
- Crates carry `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable)]`.

## Non-negotiables
- **Clean-room.** Microsoft Excel is installed on the dev machine and may be *observed* black-box: run it, use its UI with synthetic workbooks, take screenshots (by window id) stored only under `plan/excel/screenshots/`. Never read, disassemble or copy anything inside the Office bundle, never commit files produced by Excel, never copy GPL/AGPL/LGPL code (LibreOffice, Gnumeric…). Function behaviour comes from public documentation and observation.
- **Fonts live in [`KitionAI/kition-fonts`](https://github.com/KitionAI/kition-fonts)**, never in this repo. It is an optional build input (`KITION_FONTS_DIR`, default `../kition-fonts` next to this checkout): `web/scripts/build-engine.sh` copies Droid Sans Fallback from it into the kit's web build for Chinese text; without it Chinese text shows as boxes. The same checkout backs `bindings/wasm`'s `draws_chinese_with_a_font_added_at_run_time` test.
- **Shared test corpora** (real Excel-authored files) live in a separate repo (`KitionAI/kition-sheet-corpus`); never commit large binary fixtures here. Build test workbooks in code.
- **Everything is a command.** User-visible behaviour = a command in `crates/engine/engine/src/cmd/*` (id, label, ribbon path, shortcut, params doc, `enabled`, `run`) + tests. Ids follow Excel's ribbon (`home.bold`, `insert.chart`, `data.sortAscending`) plus primitives (`cell.set`, `selection.set`, `range.setValues`). The kit's editor (`web/`) and the headless kit executable both reach the same commands through `KitTools`.
- **Programmatic calls never open dialogs**: a command with empty params runs with defaults or returns an error; only menu-style invocation opens a dialog (`UiRequest::Dialog`).
- **Layering** is enforced by `cargo xtask layers`: `core`/`numfmt` (L0) → `formula`/`functions` (L1) → `model`/`calc`/`xlsx` (L2) → `chart` (L3) → `engine` (L5) → `kition-sheet-kit` (L6) → apps.
- **The UI is thin**: panels read engine state and act through `app.run(id, params)`. Colours come from `theme::Tokens`.
- **Rust only** (no handwritten JS/TS). **Never break wasm** (`cargo xtask wasm`).
- **Quality gates** before every commit: `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests, assets, layers, wasm). One task id per commit (`M2.1: borders gallery`).

## Running and looking at the app
- There is no desktop app, CLI or control channel in this repository (Kition does not use
  them). Drive the engine through `engine::Session` directly in tests, or
  through the headless kit executable: `cargo run --release -p kition-sheet`.
- For the in-page editor, run `web/` (`pnpm dev`) and use `web/dev.html` as the host.
- Shell gotcha: `mv`/`cp` are aliased interactive here — use `/bin/mv -f` / `/bin/cp -f`. macOS has no `timeout`; use `perl -e 'alarm 60; exec @ARGV' cmd`.
- Parallel agents: separate `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per agent; edit only the crates you own; delete your target dir when done.

## Roadmap
`docs/gaps.md` lists every known shortfall and `docs/roadmap.md` the order of work, both from the
feature catalogue (`features.yaml`); `docs/parity/target-app-parity.md` gives each feature's status
against Excel. The deep checklists are `docs/parity/function-parity.md`,
`docs/parity/chart-parity.md`, `docs/parity/file-format-parity.md`, `docs/parity/ui-parity.md`, `docs/parity/hardware-parity.md`,
`docs/parity/localization-parity.md`, and `docs/architecture.md`. When work lands, update the
feature in `features.yaml` and the affected docs (and their timestamp lines). `cargo xtask parity`
regenerates `docs/parity/parity-checklist.md` from `crates/engine/engine/src/catalog.rs`.
